faq_sources.topic: Should I have my new Hardeeville home's roof checked before the builder warranty ends?
answer_facts: S.C. Code 15-3-640 (official, scstatehouse.gov): suits for damages from a defective or unsafe condition of an improvement to real property may not be brought more than eight years after substantial completion; covers contract and negligence claims against builders, designers, suppliers; a certificate of occupancy (new construction) is proof of substantial completion unless contractor and owner agree a different date in writing; parties may agree before completion to a longer guarantee; building permits must carry a bold notice of the right to contract for a longer guarantee.
Short quotes: 'may be brought more than eight years after substantial completion of the improvement'; 'shall constitute proof of substantial completion of the improvement'.
Law-firm FAQ (Steinberg, plaintiff-side, not official): anyone who builds a new home 'guarantees that they performed their work properly' and sellers guarantee habitability.

NOT FOUND from an official source: that SC builders typically give a one-year workmanship warranty. The Title 39 ch. 67 'Homebuyers Protection and Warranty Act' appears only as 1990s bills; I could not confirm it was enacted. Do not state '1 year'. The warranty term is whatever the builder's written warranty says (a client/consumer fact, not public).

New-build communities in Hardeeville per Wikipedia: Hilton Head Lakes, Riverton Pointe (formerly Hampton Pointe, renamed 2021), Hearthstone Lakes, Latitude Margaritaville, Jasper County portions of Sun City Hilton Head, planned Tradition Hilton Head; New River area developments annexed into the city 2004-2010; Tradition first development agreement with the city, 2004.
sources: https://www.scstatehouse.gov/code/t15c003.php (read 2026-10-12, summarised by fetch tool; verify wording)

faq_candidates.question: Does my Hardeeville lot need an elevation certificate before or after I add to the house or re-roof?
faq_candidates.why_this_town: The City of Hardeeville publishes its own Elevation Certificate Requirements chart (05-25-2023) that depends on whether the lot or structure is in the Special Flood Hazard Area.
answer_facts: City chart: City 'reserves the right to require an elevation certificate for any project'. New construction and additions/lanai/sheds: certificate required at the stages shown (construction drawings, building under construction, finished construction) when the structure or addition is in the SFHA; not required when no portion of the lot is in the SFHA; where the SFHA only touches the building setback, a certificate is required for some stages. The chart does not mention re-roofing. Overlaps permit topic (Ridgeland owns Jasper permit FAQ) - Paul to decide.

faq_candidates.question: Which Hardeeville neighborhoods are age-restricted or master-planned, and does my roof fall under an HOA?
faq_candidates.why_this_town: Hardeeville median age 60.4; Sun City, Latitude Margaritaville and Hilton Head Lakes drove growth from 2,952 (2010) to 7,473 (2020).
answer_facts: Wikipedia: Sun City Hilton Head is age-restricted (no minimum age given on the page); Hardeeville median age 60.4 (2020); population 2,952 to 7,473. No public source I found gives any of these communities' roof/ARB rules (Latitude Margaritaville and Hilton Head Lakes searches returned nothing). So the HOA part is NOT answerable from public sources - weak.

faq_candidates.question: What building code applies to a roof in Hardeeville?
faq_candidates.why_this_town: City page posts the SC code adoption notice; BUT this is a code/permit question and the same answer applies statewide - fails portability; listed only because Hardeeville page has the official source.
answer_facts: City page: SC Building Codes Council adopted the most recent editions of the required codes, with local amendments; submittals through the online portal; special-inspections form cites IBC 2021. Contact 843-784-2231. Exact IRC edition not retrieved.
